# Ops for comparing laya's Go training step with its PyTorch reference:
#
#	cudaprof compare -ops testdata/ops/laya-torch.txt ref.pprof go.pprof
#
# The first rule that matches a kernel's name names its op.
ToBF16	bf16-cast
fmha|Flash|AttnSoftmax|SoftmaxBackward|AttnBackward|attn	attention
SplitQKV|MergeQKV|[Rr]ope	qkv-rope
nvjet|cutlass|gemm|Gemm|magma|sm80_xmma|ampere	gemm
[Ll]ayer_?[Nn]orm|GammaBeta	layernorm
GeGLU|GELU|gelu|glu	geglu
multi_tensor_apply|[Aa]dam|cudaoptim	optimizer
[Cc]at[Aa]rray|copy|Copy|Gather|gather|Scatter|index	copy-gather
reduce|Reduce|ColSum|ColumnSum|Partial|Sum	reduce
elementwise|Elementwise	elementwise
.	other

# Laya fuses into one kernel what PyTorch runs as several elementwise
# kernels. Each line below adds up an op and the kernels, or PyTorch
# elementwise functors, that do its work on the other side. The rows are
# partial: PyTorch's GeGLU gate product and RoPE's rotation run as
# MulFunctor and CUDAFunctor_add launches that no name tells apart from
# the model's other products and sums, so they stay in elementwise.
geglu = elementwise:gelu*
bf16-cast = elementwise:bfloat16_copy_kernel_cuda
qkv-rope = elementwise:neg_kernel_cuda copy-gather:*catarray*
dropout = elementwise:masked_scale_kernel other:dropout
